Samir — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: both paths work; trade-offs come down to billing simplicity, unit economics, and conversion mechanics. Below is a concise checklist plus proposals.

Checklist (one-pager):
- Prepay bucket (one invoice): immediate credits applied to calls; simpler for procurement; typically not refundable but can be converted into committed capacity at conversion with a conversion credit (we apply up to 15% of remaining prepay as conversion credit when you sign a 12+ month commit).
- Incremental top-ups: pay-as-you-go at trial rate; no upfront invoice; best if you want minimal commitment and predictable spend tied to usage spikes.
- Refunds/Transfers: standard policy — prepay for trials is non-refundable. Transfers between accounts require an approval flow (we can accommodate if you have a parent org).
- Discounting: short-term discretionary discount for one-off prepay buckets is limited; for DesignLytics I can offer a 5% one-time prepay discount or a 10% conversion credit on remaining balance upon commit (whichever you prefer).

Recommended offers tailored to you:
A) $5k prepay bucket: 5% invoice discount. Non-refundable. If you convert to a 12+ month reserved commitment within 90 days, we apply a 10% conversion credit on the unconsumed balance.
B) PAYG top-ups: no invoice discount; keep trial rates. If you convert within 30 days of top-up, we can offer a $2k conversion credit against first month of commit (applies only if commit >= $50k/yr).

Attachments: pricing snapshot and runway checklist attached. David, quick confirmation on burst capacity handling and whether we should propose a temporary concurrency bump?

Best,
